claims.statement: Moran, Ren and Kool replaced thymidine by difluorotoluene (F), an isosteric analogue without Watson-Crick hydrogen-bonding groups. In duplex DNA the analogue pairs poorly and without selectivity: against adenine it lowered the melting temperature by 12 degrees C and the stability by 3.6 kcal/mol, as much as a natural mismatch, and all four F-containing duplexes fell within 5.4 degrees C and 1.7 kcal/mol of one another. Yet the Klenow fragment inserted the activated analogue opposite template adenine with an efficiency (Vmax/Km 4.2 x 10^5) only about 40-fold below dTTP opposite adenine, and discriminated against C, G and T by 3 x 10^3 to 1 x 10^4 fold, only about 2- to 7-fold less than dTTP; elongation past the F-A pair showed only a brief pause, unlike the long pause at an abasic site. This is evidence for Hydrogen Bonds -> Template-Directed Replication of Nucleic Acids in the arising role with enabling rather than necessary necessity: template-directed copying proceeds efficiently and with high selectivity when the Watson-Crick hydrogen bonds of one base are removed, while hydrogen bonding still carries the stability and selectivity of the pairing itself.

Proteasome attribution follows the source lysate assay. No separately purified proteasome, newly isolated E1/E2/E3 requirement, new receptor-binding measurement, ATPase-step assay, translocation movie, force measurement or proteasome-inhibitor control is supplied by the selected main panels.

SDS-PAGE/autoradiography quantifies remaining full-length plus ubiquitinated forms as defined by each panel; His6 immunoblotting localizes loss of a terminal epitope. Band loss, tail clipping, complete destruction and production/reuse of free amino acids are different outcomes.

The source tests folded and methotrexate-stabilized proteins. The assays do not establish that only misfolded proteins are degraded, that native proteins are excluded, or that the proteasome itself decides whether a client is damaged.

The engineered linear Ub4 tag has four N-to-C fused ubiquitin moieties with G76V substitutions. It is not a newly measured native Lys48-isopeptide-linked polyubiquitin chain or an independently observed covalent ubiquitination reaction.

No universal requirement for ubiquitination is admitted; the paper itself cites ubiquitin-independent cases as background. Recognition, initiation, unfolding and proteolysis remain distinct, with the detailed unfolding/pulling cycle conditional.

No raw autoradiograms, numerical rate fit, binding constant, precise substrate concentration or kinetic uncertainty is reconstructed. Exact engineered tail amino-acid sequences are not printed in the reviewed main Methods, and no universal 20-residue minimum is admitted from data-not-shown observations.

The ubiquitination control adds 2 micromolar Ubal to inhibit deubiquitination and 320 micromolar methotrexate to inhibit degradation. Its accumulating ubiquitin-band signal is a net assay readout under those conditions, not direct matched receptor occupancy or one isolated E1/E2/E3 rate.

Similar source ubiquitination kinetics for full versus shortened N-end-rule tags constrain reduced tagging as the explanation for the deletion effect. They do not prove equal proteasome-binding occupancy or exact chain topology.
Selected degradation panels use 25 C and 0.5 mM ATP with regeneration; Figure 1 two-domain direction assays use 30 C and are not silently treated as the same condition.

C-terminal tail effects differ between cpLys38 and wild-type DHFR under 320 micromolar methotrexate: the former can be degraded whereas the latter can be clipped while the stabilized DHFR remains. A tag or tail does not guarantee complete degradation of every substrate.

Tail disorder is a source assignment supported by the paper separate 4 C nonspecific-protease sensitivity assay and a hydrodynamic statement partly data-not-shown. It is not a newly solved structure or an independent measurement of every tail conformation.

The global-unfolding control is a GroEL-binding/protease-protection assay at 15 C with 100 micromolar methotrexate. Degradation uses 25 C and 320 micromolar methotrexate; a similar control trace is not proof of identical local stability or kinetics under every degradation condition.

Nonspecific protease sensitivity and GroEL capture are operational readouts. A similar source global-unfolding trace does not exclude local changes or establish an exact thermodynamic free-energy identity.
The selected assays establish finite substrate susceptibility, not a newly observed persistent whole-cell quality-control property or an ontological acquisition event.

The original identify/tag/dismantle failed conformations claim is qualified to engineered tag/tail-dependent degradation of defined folded models. Universal native-versus-aberrant surveillance and selective elimination of only defective proteins are excluded from admission.

The original toxic-accumulation suppression, amino-acid recovery/reuse, aggregation prevention, maintenance of functional populations and higher-order stabilization are not measured by these band-loss/clipping assays.
Actual lysate, substrate, tag, ligand, ATP and assay conditions are retained; no universal information/gradient variable is measured.

The source lysate assays do not causally connect GroEL/GroES assistance to proteasome routing. The chaperone client assays and proteasome model substrate assays have separate systems, species preparations and contexts even though both papers use proteins called DHFR in some experiments.
N-end-rule ubiquitination and an engineered linear Ub4 fusion do not establish every phosphorylation/acetylation/methylation/glycosylation claim or universal reversibility.
Proteolytic band loss is not a new molecular electronic-structure measurement, chemistry-wide bond theory or proof of a downward-causation hierarchy.

studies.finding: With fuel, resting Na efflux averages 48 pmol/cm2 per s against a resting Na influx of 57. Removing ATP and phosphoarginine (n = 4) or applying strophanthidin (n = 1) reversibly lowers Na efflux to 10-13 pmol/cm2 per s; readmitting fuel restores it.
limitations: ATP is supplied by dialysis while the axon's own ATP production is blocked.
Fluxes, not the Na gradient, are measured; its decline is inferred from efflux falling below influx.
Few axons per condition.

studies.finding: In duplex DNA the nonpolar analog pairs poorly and without selectivity: the T-A duplex melted at 39 C with -dG25 of 12.3 kcal/mol, while replacing T by F lowered Tm by 12 C and stability by 3.6 kcal/mol, as destabilising as a natural mismatch, and all four F-containing duplexes fell within 5.4 C and 1.7 kcal/mol of one another, showing within error no thermodynamic selectivity for adenine. Nevertheless the Klenow fragment inserted dFTP opposite template A with an efficiency (Vmax/Km 4.2 x 10^5) only about 40-fold below dTTP opposite A (1.7 x 10^7), and with selectivity against C, G and T of 3 x 10^3 to 1 x 10^4 fold, only about 2- to 7-fold lower than the selectivity of dTTP; elongation past the F-A pair showed only a short-lived pause, unlike the long-lived pause at an abasic site. The authors conclude that canonical Watson-Crick hydrogen bonds are not required for efficient and high-fidelity replication and that shape complementarity is the more directly important criterion.
studies.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
limitations: One analog of one base, one polymerase (Klenow exo-) and a single sequence context; the authors state that the generality across sequence contexts and polymerases remains to be examined.
Steady-state kinetics aggregate several steps and do not identify the rate-limiting one, so the 40-fold lower insertion efficiency of dFTP is not assigned to a lost hydrogen bond.

The analog removes the Watson-Crick hydrogen-bonding groups but stacks more strongly than thymine, so hydrogen bonding and stacking are not fully separated, and whether the F-A pair adopts Watson-Crick geometry was not determined.
The hydrogen bonds of the template-primer backbone and of the enzyme to the substrate are not removed.
studies.observable: Duplex melting temperatures and free energies; qualitative single-nucleotide insertion and running-start elongation; steady-state Km, Vmax and Vmax/Km for each triphosphate-template combination
studies.preparation: Synthesise the 5'-triphosphate of the difluorotoluene nucleoside (dFTP) and 12-mer duplexes carrying a central T or F opposite A, C, G or T. Measure duplex stability by UV thermal denaturation at pH 7.0 (10 mM Na-PIPES, 100 mM NaCl, 10 mM MgCl2, 1.5 microM each strand). For replication, use 28-mer templates with a variable base and 23-mer (standing start) or 18-mer (running start) 32P-labelled primers with Klenow fragment (exo-) pretreated with inorganic pyrophosphatase; survey single-nucleotide insertions at 2 microM dNTP and run steady-state kinetics by varying dNTP concentration (5 microM duplex, 13-200 nM enzyme, 50 mM Tris pH 7.5, 10 mM MgCl2, 1 mM DTT, 0.1 mg/ml BSA, 37 C), resolving products on denaturing polyacrylamide gels. Controls: all four natural dNTPs against all four natural template bases, an abasic template and omission of dFTP from the running-start mixture.

studies.finding: DNA synthesis required ORC, DDK, CDK, pol alpha and dNTPs and depended on every firing factor including Mcm10; omission of pol alpha prevented DNA synthesis, the authors stating that all DNA synthesis requires pol alpha. Omitting C/G/UTP mainly affected the short product class attributed to repeated priming; Ctf4 omission had little effect, RPA omission removed the short products and Topo II omission reduced products longer than 600 nucleotides on circular templates. About 10 percent of input plasmid replicated, and a functional origin gave about 3.2-fold more synthesis than a mutant origin. CDK phosphorylation of ORC blocked MCM loading, phosphorylation of Sld2 and Sld3 was necessary and sufficient for CDK's activating role, and DDK acted through MCM.
limitations: Lagging-strand synthesis is incomplete: the system lacks pol delta, RFC, PCNA and Okazaki-fragment maturation.
About 10 percent of input DNA replicates on bead-attached templates.
Omission results are read from the text and figure legends; the gel images were not quantified here.
studies.observable: Labelled DNA synthesis products on alkaline agarose gels; immunoblots of firing-factor and RPA recruitment

Separate products on alkaline agarose gels. Omit single components in matched reactions, compare functional and mutant-origin templates and test kinase regulation with Sic1.
